documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

64F here to establish. Taught 2nd and 3rd grade for over thirty years, retired. Wants one doctor who answers the phone and handles her warfarin.

Atrial fibrillation: told years ago it was "here to stay"; no cardioversion attempts that she recalls. Feels an occasional flutter climbing stairs, otherwise unaware of it. No syncope, no exertional chest discomfort. Takes metoprolol succinate 100 and warfarin 5 mg nightly; INRs at her old office ran mostly in range, checked about monthly.
HTN: lisinopril 10, home cuff readings in the 120s/70s.
Lipids: rosuvastatin 20 for about a decade, tolerates it.
Knees: both ache, left more, worse after gardening and on stairs. Tylenol 650 as needed, a few times a week. Avoids NSAIDs because of the warfarin.

PSH: appendectomy 1975; hysterectomy 1998 for fibroids.
Allergies: none to medicines.
Family: father had AF and HTN, died at 81. Mother had type 2 DM and a stroke at 76. A maternal uncle had a PE after hip surgery. Sister on thyroid replacement.
Social: quit cigarettes about 9 years ago after roughly 20 pack-years. 1-2 glasses of wine a week. Lives on her own, drives, gardens.

Exam: well, pleasant. Vitals as recorded. Pulse irregularly irregular, rate controlled. Heart without murmur. Lungs clear. No JVD. No edema. Knees: bony enlargement and crepitus bilaterally, L>R, no effusion, ROM mildly reduced on the left. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. Chronic AF, rate controlled. Continue metoprolol. Warfarin 5 mg daily, goal INR 2-3; we will run her INRs here, every 4-6 weeks when stable. INR today.
2. HTN at goal. Continue lisinopril. CMP.
3. HLD on rosuvastatin 20. Lipids, CBC.
4. Knee OA. Acetaminophen as needed, stay active; keep NSAIDs off the table.
5. Former smoker, 20 pk-yr, quit ~2012. Qualifies for annual low-dose CT; she would like to think about it, will raise again at next visit.
6. Health maintenance: HCV screen today. Awaiting old records for colonoscopy, mammogram and vaccines. PHQ-2 0.
Follow up in about 4 months, sooner as needed.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Ms. Zielinski, everything from Tuesday looks good. INR is in range, so stay on 5 mg each evening and we will recheck in about 4 weeks. documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
ORTHOPAEDIC SURGERY - ADULT RECONSTRUCTION
Date of service: 05/14/2024
Referred by primary care for left knee pain.

Ms. Zielinski is a 67-year-old retired teacher with years of bilateral knee pain, left far worse over the past 6 months, now limiting walking to a couple of blocks. She has done home exercises and takes acetaminophen; NSAIDs avoided due to warfarin for atrial fibrillation.
Medications: warfarin 5 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, rosuvastatin 20 mg daily, acetaminophen as needed. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: BMI about 28. Antalgic gait. Left knee varus, crepitus, ROM 5-100, stable ligaments, neurovascularly intact.
Imaging: outside standing films reviewed, end-stage left knee OA with bone-on-bone medial compartment.
Impression: End-stage primary osteoarthritis, left knee. Conservative measures exhausted.
Plan: Left total knee arthroplasty, tentatively mid-September. Will need medical pre-operative evaluation and an anticoagulation plan from her PCP. Post-op VTE prophylaxis per hospital protocol while warfarin is held. Pre-op education class scheduled.

Orthopaedic Surgery

PRE-OP MEDICAL EVALUATION
Procedure: L TKA, scheduled 9/16/24 at the regional hospital.
Functional capacity: walks on flat ground, climbs a flight slowly limited by the knee, not by breath or chest symptoms; >4 METs by history. No chest pain, syncope, orthopnea or edema. No prior anesthesia problems (appendectomy, hysterectomy).
Meds: warfarin 5, metoprolol succ 100, lisinopril 10, rosuvastatin 20, acetaminophen PRN. NKDA.
Exam: AF, rate controlled. No murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
ECG: AF, rate 74, no acute change.
Labs drawn today: CBC, BMP, INR.
Risk: low-risk RCRI for a non-cardiac intermediate-risk procedure. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (female, age, HTN), no prior stroke/TIA.
Anticoagulation plan: last warfarin dose 9/10 (hold 5 days). No bridging given no prior thromboembolism and moderate stroke risk. INR morning of surgery per hospital. Restart warfarin per surgeon, usually evening of POD 0-1 if hemostasis OK. Post-op prophylaxis per orthopedics until INR therapeutic.
Continue metoprolol through surgery including the morning of. Hold lisinopril the morning of surgery.
She is medically optimized. Letter faxed to orthopedics.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 09/22/2024 (received with discharge summary 10/21/2024)

Chief complaint: left calf pain and swelling x 2 days.
HPI: 67F, POD 6 from left TKA at this hospital, discharged home on subcutaneous heparin 5,000 units every 8 hours for clot prophylaxis, home warfarin still on hold. Two days of aching and swelling in the left calf, separate from the knee incision pain. Denies falls or other injury. Has been up walking with PT and a walker, not bed-bound. No chest pain or shortness of breath.
PMH: chronic atrial fibrillation, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, osteoarthritis. PSH: L TKA 9/16/24, hysterectomy, appendectomy.
Meds: subcutaneous heparin as above; warfarin 5 mg (held); metoprolol succinate 100 mg; lisinopril 10 mg; rosuvastatin 20 mg; acetaminophen 650 mg q6h PRN. Allergies: NKDA on arrival.
Social: former smoker 20 pk-yr, quit ~12 yrs; wine 1-2/week; retired teacher.
Family: father AF/HTN; mother DM2 and stroke; maternal uncle with PE after hip surgery; sister hypothyroid.

Exam: Vitals stable (see flowsheet). Alert, comfortable at rest. Irregularly irregular rhythm. Lungs clear. Left knee incision clean and closed with staples. Left calf red, warm, tender; calf circumference 3 cm larger than the right. Distal pulses present.

Results: Hgb 13.2, plt 55 (250 on pre-op labs 8/27), WBC 7.8. PT 12 s, aPTT 28 s. D-dimer 2,840 ng/mL FEU (elevated). Duplex: acute L popliteal DVT.

MDM: New DVT with platelet fall of nearly 80% beginning about day 5-6 of heparin exposure. Clinical probability of HIT high. All heparin stopped, including flushes; heparin allergy flagged. PF4 antibody sent. Hematology and hospitalist consulted; start argatroban infusion. No warfarin until platelets recover.
Disposition: admitted to medicine.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received 10/21/2024 after records request)
Admitted: 09/22/2024 Discharged: 10/02/2024
Principal diagnosis: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (type II, immune-mediated) with thrombosis.
Secondary: Acute DVT, left popliteal vein. Status post left total knee arthroplasty 9/16/2024. Chronic atrial fibrillation. Hypertension. Hyperlipidemia. Osteoarthritis.

Course: Admitted from the ED POD 6 after left TKA with a left popliteal DVT and platelets 55K (from 250K preoperatively) while on subcutaneous heparin prophylaxis. Heparin discontinued on arrival. PF4/heparin antibody ELISA positive, optical density 1.84. Treated with argatroban infusion with aPTT monitoring. Platelets rose steadily, 171K by 9/27, and warfarin 5 mg nightly was resumed that day with argatroban overlap. Argatroban stopped once INR therapeutic on two consecutive days. Knee incision healing; working with PT, cleared for home with walker and home PT.
Discharge labs: platelets 212K, INR 2.4.

Allergies at discharge: HEPARIN (heparin-induced thrombocytopenia) - avoid all heparin products, including low-molecular-weight heparin and line flushes.
Discharge medications: warfarin 5 mg daily (goal INR 2-3); metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily; lisinopril 10 mg daily; rosuvastatin 20 mg daily; acetaminophen 650 mg every 6 hours as needed. Subcutaneous heparin discontinued.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with INR; orthopedics 6 weeks post-op. Anticoagulation for DVT at least 3 months, then per PCP given ongoing indication for AF.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: In the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I wanted you to know I'm back in the hospital. Had my knee done last Monday and on Sunday my calf swelled up. They found a clot behind the knee and they say the heparin shots made my platelets drop. They stopped the shots and I'm on an IV blood thinner. Nobody's told me yet when I go home. Judith

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT
Discharged 10/2 after admission 9/22 for left popliteal DVT with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, POD 6 from left TKA (9/16). Hospital summary not yet received; she brought her discharge instructions and medication list. Contact with patient made 10/3 by phone (RN).
Per patient and paperwork: subcutaneous heparin after surgery, platelets dropped, clot found, heparin stopped, IV blood thinner, then warfarin restarted; went home on warfarin 5 mg, INR 2.4 at discharge, platelets 212.
Now: calf swelling going down, still sore at the end of the day. Knee stiff, doing home PT, using walker indoors, cane outdoors. No bleeding, no chest pain, no dyspnea.
Med reconciliation: warfarin 5 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 100, lisinopril 10, rosuvastatin 20, acetaminophen PRN. Heparin injections stopped.
ALLERGY ADDED TODAY: heparin - HIT. No heparin of any kind in the future, including LMWH and flushes. Our allergy list had not been updated until this visit.
Exam: AF, rate controlled. Lungs clear. L knee incision healed, staples out, mild warmth expected post-op. L calf soft, mild residual swelling, minimal tenderness. R leg normal.
A/P
1. HIT with thrombosis, platelets recovering. CBC today.
2. Acute L popliteal DVT, provoked (surgery). Warfarin, goal 2-3, at least 3 months; continues long-term for AF anyway. INR weekly x 4, then spacing out.
3. S/p L TKA: ortho f/u 11/5.
4. AF, HTN, HLD unchanged.
Requested the full hospital record. See in 3 months, sooner if any leg or breathing change.

reports.text:
CT PULMONARY ANGIOGRAM (CT CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST)
Indication: pleuritic right chest pain, hemoptysis, hypoxia.
Technique: helical CT of the chest after IV contrast, pulmonary arterial phase.
Findings: Filling defects in the right lower lobe segmental pulmonary arteries. Main and lobar pulmonary arteries otherwise patent. Wedge-shaped peripheral area of increased opacity in the right lower lobe abutting the pleura. RV/LV ratio normal; no septal bowing or reflux of contrast to suggest right heart strain. Heart size normal. No pericardial effusion. Remaining lungs clear.
reports.conclusion: Acute right lower lobe segmental pulmonary emboli with a right lower lobe wedge-shaped opacity consistent with pulmonary infarction. No right heart strain.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 09/23/2025 (received 10/20/2025)

CC: right-sided chest pain.
HPI: 68F with chronic AF on warfarin and a history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia with left popliteal DVT about a year ago after her left knee replacement. Two hours ago, abrupt sharp pain in the right chest, much worse on a deep breath, with shortness of breath and a cough bringing up blood-streaked sputum. No fever. No trauma. No recent travel or surgery since the knee.
PMH: chronic AF; HIT type II (9/2024); L popliteal DVT 9/2024; HTN; HLD; osteoarthritis; s/p L TKA 2024.
Meds: warfarin 5 mg daily; metoprolol succinate 100 mg; lisinopril 10 mg; rosuvastatin 20 mg; acetaminophen PRN.
Allergies: HEPARIN (HIT).
Social: former smoker 20 pk-yr; wine 1-2/week; retired teacher.
Family: father AF/HTN, d. 81; mother DM2, stroke 76; maternal uncle PE after hip surgery; sister hypothyroid.

Exam: HR 110 irregular, RR 22, BP 135/85, SpO2 92% RA. Uncomfortable with breathing. Diminished breath sounds at the right base. Heart irregular, tachycardic. Legs: no swelling or erythema; right calf tender with deep palpation. L knee well healed.

Results: D-dimer 3,410 ng/mL FEU (elevated). INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic). CBC and BMP unremarkable. CTPA: RLL segmental PE with wedge-shaped RLL opacity consistent with infarct; no RV strain.

MDM: Acute PE with subtherapeutic INR on warfarin. Hypoxic on room air, not hemodynamically unstable. HEPARIN CONTRAINDICATED (HIT). Started fondaparinux 7.5 mg subcutaneously, continue warfarin. Oxygen 2 L NC.
Disposition: admit to medicine.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received 10/20/2025)
Admitted 09/23/2025, discharged 09/27/2025.
Principal diagnosis: Acute pulmonary embolism, right lower lobe segmental, with pulmonary infarction.
Contributing: subtherapeutic INR (1.6) on warfarin.
Other: chronic AF; history of HIT type II with left popliteal DVT 9/2024; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; osteoarthritis; s/p left TKA.

Course: Presented with pleuritic right chest pain, hemoptysis and hypoxia. CTPA confirmed RLL segmental emboli without RV strain. Heparin avoided given HIT. Fondaparinux 7.5 mg SC daily overlapped with warfarin 5 mg daily; fondaparinux stopped once INR at goal. Supplemental oxygen weaned on day 2. Hemoptysis stopped day 2. Pain controlled with acetaminophen.
Discharge: INR 2.3. SpO2 95% on room air at rest and with ambulation.
Allergies: HEPARIN - HIT.
Discharge medications: warfarin 5 mg daily; metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily; lisinopril 10 mg daily; rosuvastatin 20 mg daily; acetaminophen 650 mg every 6 hours as needed.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; close INR monitoring, goal 2-3.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi. I should have called sooner. Last Tuesday I woke up with a terrible pain in my right side and was coughing up a little blood. Went to the ER and they found a blood clot in my lung. They kept me until Saturday and gave me those daily shots (not heparin, they knew) until my INR came up. I'm home now and I feel weak but OK. They said see you this week. I'm sorry I missed my blood test in August. Judith

documents.title: RE: Was in the hospital
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Judith, we're glad you're home. The doctor has you Wednesday 10/1 at 1:30 with an INR at the visit. If the chest pain or breathing gets worse before then, or you cough up more than streaks of blood, call 911. We'll ask the hospital for your records.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT
Admitted 9/23-9/27 for acute right lower lobe PE, learned of it from her portal message 9/29. Records not yet received; history from patient and her discharge instruction sheet (INR at discharge 2.3, fondaparinux stopped, home on warfarin 5 mg).
Right-sided pain now only with a big breath, much less each day. No more blood in the sputum since the hospital. Winded on the stairs, better than last week. No leg pain or swelling. No bleeding.
She missed the August INR and did not rebook; INR was 1.6 in the ED.
Exam: SpO2 97% RA. HR rate controlled, irregular. Breath sounds slightly reduced R base, no rub. Calves soft, nontender, no swelling.
A/P
1. Acute PE, RLL segmental, on subtherapeutic warfarin. Continue warfarin 5 mg, goal 2-3. INR every 2 weeks for 3 months, then monthly. Reviewed: heparin never (HIT). Set up standing INR appointments on her calendar today.
2. AF, HTN, HLD unchanged.
3. LDCT deferred, she had a full chest CT in the hospital; revisit in spring.
Call right away for worse breathing, chest pain, or bleeding. Requested hospital records. Recheck 3 months.

3-month f/u after RLL PE (9/2025).
Hospital records reviewed: CTPA segmental RLL emboli with infarct, no RV strain; D-dimer 3,410; INR 1.6 on arrival.
Breathing back to where it was before. No chest pain, no hemoptysis. Walks daily. Every INR since October in range, kept every appointment.
Exam: SpO2 normal. Lungs clear throughout. AF rate controlled. No edema.
A/P
1. PE, treated, symptoms resolved. Moved to history. Warfarin 5 mg indefinitely (AF plus two clots). INR now monthly.
2. HIT history: heparin allergy, permanent.
3. AF, HTN, HLD stable.
4. Lung screening: due; ordered LDCT for April.
Next visit May.
